title: Stream fragmentation and cancel-safe iterator patterns for Go SDK streaming client
creator: Aisha Patel
acceptance_criteria: Introduce StreamIterator API that returns (Message, error) and supports io.EOF to indicate clean end-of-stream
Canceling the parent context must immediately unblock Recv()/Next() with context.Canceled and no leaked goroutines in 30s stress test
Partial-fragment assembly must be performed inside the SDK; callers receive assembled logical messages, not raw frames
Resume token flow must respect the parent's context deadline: no retry/backoff goroutine should outlive parent context unless explicitly detached
Add integration tests that simulate network stalls, mid-message cancels, and server-injected resume points
Update README + Go examples demonstrating common patterns (graceful shutdown, timeouts, streaming fan-in)
technical_notes:
Design highlights and decisions:

1) Single responsible goroutine model: create one internal reader goroutine per StreamIterator which owns the underlying transport reads and performs frame reassembly. It writes fully assembled messages into a bounded channel (capacity 16). The public Recv/Next pulls from that channel.

2) Cancellation propagation: attach a cancelable child context to the internal reader (ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parentCtx)). When Recv returns due to user cancellation, call cancel() immediately and drain channels in a short, deterministic window to avoid goroutine leaks. Use sync.Once to ensure cancel is idempotent.

3) Deadline semantics: if parentCtx has a deadline, the internal reader uses per-read deadlines set on the transport. We differentiate between transport-level timeout and context cancellation using errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) vs net.Error.Timeout(). Provide wrapper errors: ErrContextCanceled, ErrStreamTimedOut, ErrNetworkEOF.

4) Fragmentation and assembly: frames carry a header (seq, is_last). The reader accumulates fragments into a bytes.Buffer until is_last==true, then decodes into the application Message. If parentCtx is canceled mid-assembly, the partial buffer is discarded and assembly state cleared.

5) Resume tokens: store the last completed-message offset. Resume attempts are performed synchronously from Recv() if the transport indicates a recoverable transient. Background retry goroutines are avoided unless the caller explicitly opts in via a WithDetachedRetries option. This ensures no background goroutines outlive the caller context inadvertently.

6) Backpressure: bounded channel capacity plus a non-blocking drop metric path. When channel is full we either block upstream reads (preferred) or return a specific ErrBackpressure if configured with WithNonBlockingMode.

7) Observability: surface metrics for assembly-latency, fragments-per-message, dropped-messages, and active-iterators. Link to Console metrics: streaming/assembly-latency.
implementation_plan: Create new type StreamIterator in internal/streaming/iterator.go with constructor NewStreamIterator(ctx, transport, opts...)
Implement internal reader goroutine that performs frame reads, per-read deadlines, and message assembly
Define error values ErrContextCanceled, ErrStreamTimedOut, ErrNetworkEOF, ErrBackpressure in errors.go
Add tests: unit tests for assembly edge-cases, race-detector builds for goroutine leaks, and integration harness that simulates stalls
Update public SDK docs and examples in examples/streaming/ and README.md
Open PR and request review from eng-infra + client-sdk leads
testing_plan: Unit: simulate frames arriving out-of-order, mid-message cancel: assert no goroutine leaks (use runtime.NumGoroutine baseline) and error == context.Canceled
Integration: local test server that intentionally stalls after first fragment; ensure caller cancel returns quickly (<50ms) and reader goroutine exits
Stress: 10k concurrent iterators created/destroyed over 5 minutes to surface leaks
Regression: add to CI a race-detector job that runs the main assembly tests
Observability: validate metrics emitted to prometheus pushgateway in integration harness
rollout_notes:
Ship behind a feature flag: GO_SDK_STREAM_ITERATOR=1. Enable flag for internal dogfood org first, then beta customers. Timeline: 
1) Merge and enable for internal org for two weeks. 
2) Monitor assembly-latency and goroutine count dashboards. 
3) Gradually roll to 10% hosted traffic, watch for ErrBackpressure spikes. 
4) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable signals.

If customers need backward-compatible behaviour, provide WithLegacyFrameMode option that returns raw frames instead of assembled messages.

notes_for_review:
Points reviewers should focus on: 
- Correct differentiation of error types (context vs transport) and public doc language. 
- Potential goroutine leak paths during reconnects/resume flow. 
- Backpressure behavior default (block vs error) and whether we should opt for blocking by default. 
- API ergonomics: NewStreamIterator(ctx, ...) vs stream.Recv(ctx) — we chose constructor variant to make cancellation explicit and centralize lifecycle.
